PullRequest.Title: extensions: share uninstall command with Agents window
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #349483

cc @alexr00 @aeschli

## Summary

Uninstalling an extension-contributed plugin in Agents fails because `workbench.extensions.uninstallExtension` is registered only in the Editor. Move the unchanged registration into the Extensions actions module shared by both windows.

This affects the owning-extension removal path, not canvases specifically or every plugin. The existing confirmation asks to uninstall the owning VS Code extension; confirming removes the extension and its bundled features, while Cancel retains it. Confirmation wording and uninstall behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

- Build, client type-check, changed-file lint, and 34 targeted uninstall tests passed.
- Real Windows Code OSS checks in Agents and Editor: Cancel retains the owning extension; confirmation removes it and its plugin, verified against installed-extension inventory.
- Used an installed skills-only fixture exercising the same ownership route, not the actual Agent Plan binary. All-profiles and dependent-extension prompts were not tested live.

**Before**

![Before: missing uninstall command in Agents](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d54e5ada-b192-4365-9d56-2434486cc50d)

**After: cancel and successful uninstall**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/479e2e24-19dc-4660-b5f5-39e1ed9eafa8

<details>
<summary>Validation commands (all passed)</summary>

```powershell
pnpm run build-fast
pnpm run typecheck-client
pnpm run oxlint src\vs\workbench\contrib\extensions\browser\extensionsActions.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\extensions\browser\extensions.contribution.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\extensions\test\electron-browser\extensionsActions.test.ts
.\scripts\test.bat --isolate --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\extensions\test\electron-browser\extensionsActions.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\agentPluginActions.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\extensions\test\browser\agentsWindowExtensionsWidget.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\extensions\test\browser\agentsWindowExtensionPage.test.ts --grep "[Uu]ninstall" --reporter dot
```

</details>

Scenarios.Scenario: Editor and Agents window startup and extension-action module loading
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing static imports load extensionsActions.ts before contribution registration completes. The added code registers command metadata and a handler; service acquisition, installed-extension enumeration, and uninstall work remain inside the handler and do not run during registration.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One registration per loaded module/window, independent of installed-extension count, plugin count, action instances, or rendered rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous, constant-size registry insertion. No tasks or boundary calls are launched by the moved registration.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Normal module evaluation is once per window. Editor previously imported extensionsActions.ts from extensions.contribution.ts; Agents already imported it through agentsWindowExtensionsWidget.ts and agentsWindowExtensionsMarketplace.ts. No new heavyweight module dependency or cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete diff shows a verbatim handler relocation, the unchanged import chains establish prior module loading, and CommandsRegistry.registerCommand only wraps/stores the handler and emits registration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No runtime startup measurements; the only additional Agents startup work established by the diff is constant-size command registration.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Editor loses the original registration and gains the identical registration in its already-imported actions module. Agents gains one bounded registry entry in a module it already loaded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Explicit uninstall command in the Editor, including unknown and built-in identifiers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Command activation, getInstalled across configured extension-management servers, identifier validation, and uninstall completion are awaited in that order. Missing identifiers are rejected before service enumeration; unknown and built-in identifiers stop after enumeration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request installed-extension inventories and transform the returned extensions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inventory request per configured server, normally one local server or local plus remote; not one request per extension. Unknown or built-in identifiers perform the same single inventory round and no uninstall round.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The deleted Editor registration invoked the same service method once with the same arguments and awaited the same inventories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All configured-server inventories must finish before the handler selects its target.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read profile membership and extension manifests/localization data, resolve extension directories, and construct local-extension records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Collection-wide scan work scales with installed extensions in each server/profile. User manifests and directory resolutions can scale with inventory size; concurrent scans with the same profile/language share their scan promise, but each caller still constructs local records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical full-inventory scan and conversion path in the Editor command before relocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Inventory scanning and record construction must finish before target validation. Workspace inventories await their existing initializePromise and subsequently filter retained records.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send grouped uninstall requests to the owning extension-management server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For a normal single extension, one owning-server uninstall request. Pack processing occurs within that request; special multiserver behavior is addressed separately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The original handler called the same uninstall method with the same extension and default options.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The handler awaits service uninstall completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scan installed user extensions for pack/dependency checks, read profile membership, and write updated profile JSON.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached user-inventory scan per distinct profile within an uninstall invocation; one profile update per deduplicated uninstall task, including packed extensions when applicable. Each update processes the profile collection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same grouping, per-invocation profile cache, task deduplication, JSON serialization, and profile writes already served Editor command invocations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Validation and queued profile writes complete before uninstall resolves.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Report gallery uninstall statistics with an HTTP POST when the extension has a gallery UUID and the gallery manifest exposes a statistics resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one statistics POST per newly executed uninstall task; skipped without a gallery UUID/resource or on web.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same optional awaited reporting already occurred for successful Editor command uninstalls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing task awaits statistics reporting before completing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Optionally execute an extension uninstall script and remove extension storage when physical cleanup removes the extension.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: No direct lifecycle subprocess in the default UninstallExtensionInProfileTask, which removes profile membership. Later physical cleanup may execute a declared hook per deleted extension.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same profile-removal task and subsequent physical-cleanup ownership existed before the move.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Physical cleanup is not added to the command handler by this diff; the existing lifecycle path limits hook processes to five.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed inventories across the configured servers, workspace-extension count, and the deduplicated owner/pack tasks. Ordinary user invocation targets one extension, not every installed item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Server inventories run concurrently through Promise.all. Manifest scans and local-record conversion use Promise.all; membership accesses serialize through a per-profile Queue. Uninstall tasks run concurrently after dependency validation and wait for opposite install tasks when necessary. All scheduling is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No command-level positive or negative inventory cache is added or removed. Native scanning coalesces in-flight scans by profile/language and clears promises on settlement; this user-scan path does not request the persistent useCache option. Uninstall caches inventories per profile within the invocation and joins existing tasks keyed by extension/profile/version. Workspace inventory initialization is shared.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: deleted and added handlers are identical, service decorators resolve to the same workbench service, and the service/IPC/scanner/task implementations establish the exact boundary cardinality and scheduling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Inventory sizes, filesystem speed, remote latency, pack size, and gallery response time are not measured. These affect existing uninstall duration, not a newly introduced mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The existing collection-wide reads, allocations, optional network wait, and cleanup path are unchanged; relocation neither increases invocation frequency nor defeats batching or caching.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remove an extension-contributed plugin from Agents, accepting or cancelling the owning-extension prompt
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing plugin remove callback first awaits confirmation. Cancel returns without executing the command. Confirmation executes the now-registered uninstall command and awaits inventory selection and owning-extension removal before returning success.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate inventories and submit uninstall to the owning server through the shared command.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cancel: zero inventory/uninstall calls. Confirm: one inventory request per configured server followed by grouped uninstall requests, normally one owning-server request. Multiple bundled plugin features do not independently invoke the command during this operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agents already attempted the command after confirmation, but it was not registered there; CommandService followed its unknown-command activation path and ultimately failed without reaching the uninstall handler. The diff makes the existing user-requested operation executable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The accepted removal action waits for the normal uninstall service path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform standard inventory scans and profile-membership updates for owning-extension removal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same installed-inventory and deduplicated-task scaling as the Editor command; no per-plugin scan or removal loop is added. Cancel issues none.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The missing Agents command prevented these uninstall-service operations. Editor and other extension-uninstall entry points already used this implementation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Accepted removal awaits the standard inventory and profile-update work; plugin-source discovery itself is not changed or invoked by command registration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Optionally report gallery uninstall statistics for executed owner/pack tasks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one POST per executed task with a gallery UUID and statistics resource; none on cancelled removal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The failing Agents command never reached reporting. The newly reachable path uses the unchanged standard uninstall service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing uninstall completion awaits eligible reports.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicitly selected extension-contributed plugin maps to one owning extension. Installed-extension inventory and any owning extension pack control service cost, not the total number of plugin cards or bundled features.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Confirmation gates issuance. Once accepted, configured-server scans and normal service tasks follow the existing concurrent/grouped implementation; per-profile file writes remain serialized. No automatic fan-out from startup, rendering, or discovery is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Same existing shared service, scan coalescing, per-profile inventory cache, workspace initialization, and task deduplication as Editor. No new retained plugin metadata, polling, failure retry loop, or per-plugin cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the sole production call site supplies one extensionId after confirmed dialogue, the source remove closure is per selected plugin, and the moved handler has unchanged service calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agents inventory size and uninstall durations are unmeasured. Enabling the intended operation has inherent cost, but there is no evidenced gratuitous amplification.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The diff newly enables necessary work for an explicit operation that previously failed, rather than adding redundant work or placing uninstall on a hotter path. Cancellation remains boundary-free.

Scenarios.Scenario: Uninstall with remote servers, language-pack replicas, application-scoped extensions, or packed extensions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial server inventories finish before target selection. Remote dependent checks and language-pack replica lookup occur before grouped uninstall requests. Application-scope profile discovery and pack/dependent validation precede parallel task execution and queued profile updates.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read inventories from configured servers, check remote dependents, locate language-pack copies, and submit grouped server uninstalls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Initial inventory: one request per server. Local removal with remote present adds one remote-user inventory check for the single selected extension. Language-pack removal reads each other server once to locate its copy and sends at most one grouped uninstall per affected server; on desktop there are normally at most local and remote servers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical for Editor command invocations. Agents newly gains this existing required service behavior only after explicit confirmation; relocation does not change its cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Replica discovery and remote dependency checks are awaited; server uninstall requests then execute concurrently.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scan applicable profiles, identify packed extensions, and rewrite profile membership for each distinct task.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Profile inventory is cached per distinct profile within each server invocation, not fetched for every pack member. Application-scoped extension handling may visit configured profiles; task keys deduplicate extension/profile/version combinations. Profile writes scale with executed task count and membership size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cross-profile rules, pack expansion, profile cache, task keys, and profile-write serialization existed before the move.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Profile discovery/validation precedes task execution; same-profile membership reads and writes serialize through the existing queue.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Report eligible uninstall statistics for tasks across affected servers/profiles and pack members.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one eligible POST per newly executed deduplicated task; no new per-installed-extension reporting is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical task-level reporting in the Editor service path; Agents reaches it only because its requested uninstall now succeeds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Parallel task completion still awaits existing reporting.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of configured servers, configured profiles for application-scoped extensions, installed inventory per profile, and deduplicated owner/pack tasks. These differ from the number of visible plugin features.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Initial server scans run concurrently; language-pack replica reads and cross-profile discovery are awaited while collecting tasks. Grouped server uninstalls and distinct tasks run concurrently; same-profile file accesses serialize, and opposite install tasks are awaited. No global scan limiter is added or removed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Within-invocation installedExtensionsMap groups reads by profile, native scan promises coalesce overlapping same-profile/language scans, and uninstallingExtensions joins existing same-key tasks and removes entries in finally. No cache key, invalidation, negative-cache policy, or lifetime is changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected server grouping, remote-check loop, profile inventory map, task-key deduplication, parallel execution, and profile queue directly establish effective cardinality and concurrency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Prevalence of large packs, many profiles, and remote sessions is unknown; all scaling mechanisms examined here are unchanged rather than introduced by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Potentially scaling multiserver/profile/pack costs belong to the unchanged authoritative uninstall implementation. The diff does not multiply requests by plugin features, remove task deduplication, or alter scheduling.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all three changed files and every diff page against base ddbdd50a9ed1f9dc32e4fbadcf950b290e7d35b4. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression found. Production changes relocate an identical deferred handler into a module already loaded by both window types; the newly reachable Agents uninstall remains an explicit, confirmation-gated operation using existing grouped services. Added tests introduce no product hot-path work. No sufficiently proven performance-regression fix with introducing-commit provenance was identified. Static review only; no runtime duration measurements.
